title: Assays for studying Listeria-Containing Vacuoles
author: Hélène erne
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.kwmcxc6
materials: 5 • Prepare the primary antibodies solution by diluting rabbit polyclonal L. monocytogenes antibodies and mouse LAMP1 monoclonal antibodies in PBS with 2% BSA. Maintain the antibody solution on ice. • Prepare an incubation chamber, with a wet Whatman paper and a parafilm on it (firmly stick to the Whatman and without any bubble). Mark the parafilm with a number to correspond to a coverslip (Note 7). • Dispatch drops of 40 μl of the antibody solution on the parafilm, for each coverslip. Use a fine tip forceps to pick up the coverslip and return the coverlip on the primary antibody (i.e. the cell face on the antibody solution), and incubate for 60 min. • Prepare the secondary antibody solution by diluting the secondary AlexaFluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit antibody (1:400), and Cy3-conjugated (or Alexa Fluor 555-conjugated) anti-mouse antibody (1:400), DAPI or Hoechst (1:1000) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated phalloidin (1:400) in PBS supplemented with 2% BSA (Note 8). • Gently detach each coverslip by injecting PBS under it. Wash the coverslip in three successive bathes of PBS. • Place the coverslip (cell side down) on a drop of 40 μl of the secondary antibody solution dispatched on a parafilm in the incubation chamber. Incubate for 30 min at room temperature in the dark to protect the fluorescent probes. • Gently detach each coverslip by injecting PBS under it. Wash the coverslip in two successive bathes of PBS and one bath of distilled water. • Remove excess water by touching the edge of the coverslip to a paper towel and mount the coverslip with 10 μL mounting medium onto a glass slide. Avoid forming bubbles. • Let the coverslip dry overnight at room temperature, in the dark to protect the fluorescent probes. • Acquire images in the 350 nm (DAPI/Hoechst, to visualize nuclei and bacterial DNA), 488 nm (L. monocytogenes), 546 nm (LAMP1), and 647 nm (F-actin) channels on an inverted motorized fluorescence microscope, equipped with a digital camera. Use a 40X (or 20X) objective to observe bacterial spreading in the cell monolayer, and 100X (or 63X) objectives to observe Listeria-Containing Vacuoles (LisCVs). LisCVs appear as perinuclear LAMP1-positive compartments containing F-actin-negative L. monocytogenes. 3.4) Assessment of the integrity of intravacuolar bacteria using the LIVE/DEAD® BacLight(TM) Viability Assay We adapted the Live/Dead BacLight Bacterial Viability assay from references [7] and [8], to assess whether bacteria in LisCVs have intact or damaged membranes. This assay is based on the discriminative labeling of two fluorescent nucleic acid-stains: the green membrane-permeant dye SYTO9 and the red membrane-impermeant dye propidium iodide (PI), which only crosses damaged cell membranes. Both dyes penetrate dead cells, but SYTO9 fluorescence is reduced in presence of PI. As such, intact bacteria appear green, while those with damaged membranes appear red.

steps.title: Prepare JEG3 cell culture
steps.instruction: Thaw a frozen JEG3 aliquot at least one week before infection, resuspend in 10 mL MEM‑10% FBS medium in a 15 mL tube, centrifuge 5 min at 200 × g, discard supernatant, resuspend the pellet in 10 mL warm medium, seed into a 75 cm² flask and incubate at 37 °C with 10 % CO₂; subculture when cells reach ~80 % confluency.

steps.title: Prepare Listeria stock
steps.instruction: At least three days before infection, streak L. monocytogenes strain 10403S from frozen glycerol stock onto a BHI agar plate and incubate 48 h at 37 °C; store plates at 4 °C for up to 15 days if needed.

steps.title: Seed cells for infection
steps.instruction: Two (or four) days prior to infection, trypsinize JEG3 cells, count, and seed 2 mL per well into 6‑well plates (add sterilized 22 mm coverslips if performing staining assays) to obtain 90–100 % confluency at infection (aim for 1 × 10⁵–2 × 10⁵ cells/well for a 2‑day schedule or 1 × 10⁴–3 × 10⁴ cells/well for a 4‑day schedule). Prepare three wells for initial cell counting and three wells for final counting. Incubate at 37 °C, 10 % CO₂ for the indicated 2 or 4 days.

steps.title: Prepare overnight bacterial culture
steps.instruction: The day before infection inoculate a single colony into 5 mL BHI broth in a 15 mL tube, seal, and grow overnight at 37 °C with shaking.

steps.title: Prepare bacterial inoculum
steps.instruction: On the infection day, take 1 mL of the overnight culture, centrifuge 2 min at 10 600 × g, discard supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 1 mL PBS. Dilute this suspension in MEM to obtain an inoculum of 2 mL per well that delivers an MOI of ~0.1 (≈4 × 10⁴–8 × 10⁴ bacteria per 2 mL for wells containing 4 × 10⁵–8 × 10⁵ cells). Verify the MOI by plating serial dilutions on BHI agar and incubating 48 h at 37 °C. Keep three non‑infected wells for later cell counting.

steps.title: Infect cells and synchronize uptake
steps.instruction: Aspirate medium from each well, add 2 mL warm MEM, then add 2 mL bacterial inoculum. Centrifuge the plate 2 min at 300 × g to synchronize bacterial entry. Transfer the plate to the 37 °C, 10 % CO₂ incubator and allow invasion for 1 h.

steps.title: Gentamicin treatment and incubation
steps.instruction: After the 1‑h invasion, gently wash cells twice with 2 mL pre‑warmed MEM per well. Replace MEM with 2 mL complete MEM supplemented with 25 µg/mL gentamicin and return the plate to the incubator for 3 days. (If using a higher MOI (1–10), first treat with 2 mL MEM containing 100 µg/mL gentamicin for 10 min, wash, then add medium with 25 µg/mL gentamicin.)

steps.title: Quantify intracellular bacteria by CFU
steps.instruction: After 3 days, aspirate medium and wash cells gently with 1 mL pre‑warmed MEM. Lyse cells by adding 1 mL cold distilled water per well, incubate 10 min on ice (4 °C), scrape the monolayer and pipette up/down five times to ensure complete lysis.

substeps.instruction: Make a 1:10 dilution by mixing 100 µL lysate with 900 µL PBS; then prepare 1:100 and 1:1000 dilutions sequentially.
Spread 50 µL of each dilution onto a 10 cm BHI agar plate (three separate sectors per plate). Let the drops dry a few minutes under the hood, then incubate plates 48 h at 37 °C.
Count colonies on the dilution yielding 10–100 colonies and calculate CFU per well.

Normalize CFU to cell number: from the three reserved wells detach cells with 250 µL Trypsin/EDTA for 5 min, add 250 µL MEM (total 500 µL), mix, take 20 µL and add 20 µL 0.4 % (w/v) Trypan Blue (1:2 dilution). Count viable (non‑blue) and non‑viable (blue) cells with a hemocytometer (do not keep cells in Trypan Blue >10 min). Compute CFU per cell.

steps.title: Immunofluorescence staining of LisCVs
steps.instruction: Use 22 mm square coverslips sterilized 2 h at 180 °C. After 3 days infection, remove medium and wash cells with 1 mL PBS. Fix by adding 1 mL 4 % paraformaldehyde in PBS, incubate 30 min at room temperature in a chemical fume hood. Remove fixative and wash twice with 1 mL PBS. Permeabilize with 1 mL 0.4 % Triton X‑100 in PBS for 4 min. Wash three times with 2 mL PBS. Block by adding 1 mL PBS containing 2 % BSA per well. (Proceed with primary and secondary antibody incubations as required, keeping coverslips wet at all times.)

steps.title: Live/Dead BacLight viability assay
steps.instruction: Following the 3‑day infection, process each coverslip separately. Wash twice with 1 mL MOPS/MgCl₂ solution (0.1 M MOPS, pH 7.4, 1 mM MgCl₂). Add 1 mL Live/Dead staining solution (1.6 µM SYTO 9, 20 µM propidium iodide, 0.1 % Triton X‑100 in MOPS/MgCl₂). Centrifuge the plate 10 min at 300 × g to keep cells attached, then incubate 5 min at room temperature in the dark. Wash twice with 1 mL MOPS/MgCl₂ solution. Mount the coverslip on a glass slide, seal with clear nail polish, and incubate 2 min at 37 °C. Immediately examine under a fluorescence microscope (63× or 100×) for up to 10 min; bacteria appear as green (SYTO 9) or red (PI) filaments.
